chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi from al-Hasan ibn Sayf from his brother from his father from Muhammad ibn Ayyub from Rifah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The head of the year is the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr); in it is written what will occur from the year to the year.

key_terms.مِنَ السَّنَةِ إِلَى السَّنَةِ: From the year to the year

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Laylat al-Qadr as the 'head of the year' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies Laylat al-Qadr as the 'head of the year,' signifying its pivotal role in the cosmic decree. In Shia scholarly tradition, this night is viewed as the moment when the broad outlines of the coming year's events are inscribed, establishing a spiritual and metaphysical link between the current and subsequent years. This concept underscores the night's importance not just as a singular event of worship, but as a foundational moment for annual destiny.
